exposure: Maternal Staphylococcus aureus (Sa) nasal colonization status
outcome: Anti-Staphylococcus aureus (Sa) IgG levels in maternal and cord sera
Anti-Staphylococcus aureus (Sa) IgG1 levels in maternal and cord sera
Anti-Staphylococcus aureus (Sa) IgG2 levels in maternal and cord sera
IgG avidity indexes in maternal and cord sera
cohort: The study included 250 parturients, with 49 nasally colonized with S. aureus (case group) and 98 non-colonized subjects (control group), along with their newborns.
finding: Maternal Sa nasal colonization at delivery was not associated with higher anti-Sa antibody levels in the mother or newborns, but the presence of Sa-specific IgA in colostrum reinforces the importance of breastfeeding.
